answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so an agent’s voting weight depends on paths from trusted seeds rather than self-created identities. If a Sybil cluster, including identities named opal, jade, and saffron, has few edges to the honest graph, its low conductance limits the probability that walks enter it. Under bounded degree and seed-weight assumptions, min-cut and transitivity bounds therefore cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight.
